status_summary: The Ensuring Accurate and Complete Abortion Data Reporting Act of 2025 was introduced in both chambers on 2025-01-22 (H.R. 627, referred to Energy and Commerce, and S. 178, referred to Finance); it would make certain Medicaid family planning payments depend on annual state abortion data submissions to CDC. CDC's surveillance page (updated November 2024) says state reporting is voluntary with no national requirement. In September 2025 a public radio outlet reported an unsigned CDC email saying CDC was pausing analysis and would not release an abortion surveillance report, and in December 2025 CNN reported the annual report was delayed until spring 2026, with HHS and a former CDC official giving different explanations. An advocacy news site reported in July 2026 that no report on 2023 data had appeared and that the CDC director nominee called abortion surveillance critical.

timeline.event: Ensuring Accurate and Complete Abortion Data Reporting Act of 2025 introduced in the House as H.R. 627 and referred to Energy and Commerce; Senate companion S. 178 introduced the same day and referred to Finance.
Public radio reports a CDC email, obtained by FOIA, saying CDC is pausing abortion data analysis and will not release an abortion surveillance report.
CNN reports CDC's annual abortion report is delayed until spring amid staffing turmoil; states still submit data voluntarily.
Advocacy news site reports that the CDC director nominee described abortion surveillance as critical at her confirmation hearing and that no report on 2023 data had been released.

title: Require states to report abortion data to CDC and pass the abortion data reporting bill
